editorial.headline: Government-Run Training, Closed to Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: Government-run, non-school training can span administrative, technical, health and adult learning—but this activity is closed to foreign investment nationally and cannot be registered by PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85550 is the lane for government-organised education outside the school system: courses and training intended to add or support skills and competence. Its scope is deliberately broad, taking in administrative-staff courses, training for senior administrative staff, competence development for teachers and education personnel, technical training centres, beauty courses—from body care to bridal make-up—and household-welfare instruction in sewing, cooking and nutrition. It also reaches health-related teaching, including first aid, massage and acupuncture, education on nuclear-related subjects, other courses, and adult business-learning groups.

That breadth should not be mistaken for a blank cheque. The activity is defined by its public organiser—government—and the slim record identifies no business scale as open. It contains no separate opening that would justify assigning a particular scale or wider type of registrant. The important point is simple: this is a government-run, out-of-school education category whose content can be practical, vocational and adult-facing, yet whose investment treatment is set by the same record, not by the apparent familiarity of any individual course.

Nationally, the answer is unequivocal. Its PMA status is TERTUTUP, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 0%. A foreign investor therefore has no permitted ownership stake under the national entry shown here. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. This is not a partial opening, nor does the wide range of subject matter create a different foreign-investment outcome: the record’s national status is closed.

Bali calls for a careful distinction, not an optimistic loophole. The Bali status is also TERTUTUP, and the record expressly marks the activity as blocked for PMA registration. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. Its listed risk position is medium-high/high, so it is not blocked by the island-wide Bali moratorium that applies to all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI for PMA; the record still requires address-specific verification. That does not reverse the Bali result. The moratorium is not the cited reason for the block, while the Bali status and block flag remain decisive. A wide curriculum does not change the clean conclusion: the activity is closed nationally and closed in Bali.
